To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the geometric representation of the open string model can be constructed using a scheme of "surfaces and lines" of Faraday and that a consistent geometric representation can be built only if the charge of the string is quantized.

(1) The geometric representation for the open-string theory can be built using ``surfaces and Faraday lines'', (2) This geometric representation leads to a consistent quantization of the model, provided that the string charge is a quantized multiple of 2π, and (3) The quantized open-string theory can also be described in terms of a non-commutative algebra, which is a natural generalization of the Loop Representation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the geometric quantization of open strings in the context of a model with non-trivial topology.
a geometric quantization of open-strings interacting with Abelian gauge-fields.
the geometric quantization of a system of interacting open-strings in a background field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in this model, there exists a consistent quantization of the open-string degrees of freedom using a geometric representation, and that the quantization of the coupling constant is necessary to achieve this.
the quantization of the non-relativistic open-string is achieved by means of a ``geometrization'' of the theory, and the quantized charge is a natural outcome of the geometric-representation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in this model, the quantization condition for the coupling constant is the same as the quantization condition of the electric charge of a charged particle in Quantum Electrodynamics.
we have quantized the open strings in a geometric representation using a generalized loop representation.
the quantization of non-relativistic strings in a geometric representation is possible, provided that the coupling constants are quantized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the quantization condition for the charge is not a consequence of the gauge symmetry but rather a consequence of the quantization of the area of the surfaces of the Faraday lines.

the quantization of non-relativistic strings is a natural generalization of the quantization of relativistic ones, in the same way that the non-relativistic limit of a relativistic theory is a generalization of a non-relativistic theory.
the quantization of non-relativistic open strings is a natural consequence of the quantization of their coupling constant.
